senses.gloss:
hiṁsā
(‘violence’)
------------------------------------------
Hinduism has always considered moral purity as a prerequisite of spiritual quest and perfection. Among the moral disciplines strongly recommended, अहिṁसा or non-violence gets the primary place.
Since अहिṁसा has been defined as not injuring any living being either physically or by harsh words or even by inimical thoughts, the opposite of this can be considered as हिṁसा or violence. So हिṁसा is any act that hurts a person’s body or मिन्द्, whether it ultimately causes his death or not.
The Hindu scriptures (vide योग-sūtras of पतञ्जलि 2.34) go to the extent of telling us that हिṁसा, whether perpetrated directly or caused to be perpetrated by others or even approved of, when committed by others, is a sin and must be eschewed. Such persons go to हेल्ल् and suffer terribly for a long time.
However, immolation of animals in वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस् or हिṁसा committed by one under attack, for saving one’s life and limb, are not considered as हिṁसा.
